title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Post-Award Formalities - Debriefings
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: The primary objective of conducting a supplier debriefing with an unsuccessful proposer is to:
options: Convince them not to file a protest
Negotiate a secondary backup contract just in case the winner defaults
Provide constructive feedback regarding the strengths and weaknesses of their proposal based on the evaluation rubric to help them improve future submissions
Allow them to see the confidential trade secrets of the winning proposal
questions.explain: A debriefing is an educational meeting. It explains to the vendor exactly how their proposal was scored against the evaluation criteria, highlighting areas where they lost points so they can be more competitive next time.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: During a post-award debriefing, a losing vendor aggressively asks, 'Why did Vendor X score higher than me on the technical approach?' How should the procurement officer respond?
options: Read the winning vendor's technical proposal aloud to prove it was better
Decline to compare proposals directly; reiterate that debriefings only focus on the specific strengths and weaknesses of the requesting vendor's own proposal
Agree that the scoring was probably flawed but state that the decision is final
Allow the vendor to read the evaluators' personal notes
questions.explain: A critical rule of debriefings is that they are not a forum for point-by-point comparisons between competitors. The discussion must strictly revolve around the vendor's own proposal and why it received the scores it did.
